A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RSPO research. Their text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. v1 has no appendices; v2's Appendices A–E are complete and readable.

before.justification: v1 reports original Countdown training and ablation experiments and Qwen3-30B-A3B mathematical reasoning results in Table 1 and Figures 2–5.

after.justification: v2 retains original Countdown and mathematics experiments and adds code benchmark results, training diagnostics and throughput measurements.

M1.justification: v1 Section 3.2 and Equation (5) apply router-shift weighting after token-level clipping. v2 Section 4.2 and Equations (9)–(11) multiply the weight into the importance ratio before clipping and aggregation. This changes the central objective and clipping decisions. The router-shift statistic, flooring and stop-gradient already existed.

E1.justification: Countdown and the five mathematics benchmarks are retained. v2 adds code training using PrimeIntellect, LeetCode, TACO and LiveCodeBench, with evaluation on LiveCodeBench, MBPP and HumanEval, substantially extending task and domain coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Base, GRPO, GSPO and GMPO. The corresponding plug-in comparison expands from GRPO/GSPO with and without router shift in v1 Figure 4 to include GMPO with and without router shift in v2 Figure 4. The freezing and replay comparators remain in Appendix D.

E3.justification: v1 specifies a global batch size of 128 across experiments; v2 Appendix A.1 reports 256 for the small-scale setting and retains 128 at large scale. Countdown plots cover longer horizons and report training reward instead of the earlier validation trajectories. Added code protocols include 32K-token generation and LiveCodeBench v4–v5 evaluation with training data described as preceding v5.

E4.justification: v2 adds comparative routing-severity, importance-ratio and clipping diagnostics in Figure 5, efficiency analysis in Section 5.6, and expanded plug-in stability testing. Floor sensitivity, stop-gradient and freezing/replay analyses already appeared in v1; their appendix placement does not establish new experiments.

E5.justification: v2 Sections 5.1–5.2 newly report means over three random seeds for training curves and results. Both versions specify 32 repeated AIME24 evaluations. This adds seed-count disclosure without establishing an increase in runs; no confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is added.

E6.justification: All mathematics values in Table 1 are retained, including RSPO's 77.1 average. Added code results give RSPO an 85.2 average versus GMPO's 82.5. v2 also adds or revises reward, entropy and diagnostic trajectories, reports a 20.8% throughput reduction relative to GMPO, and estimates approximately 1.5 GiB of routing-cache memory.

T1.justification: The formal update changes from post-clipping weighting in v1 Equation (5) to pre-clipping ratio rescaling in v2 Equation (11), and Equation (8) defines a router-shift clipping-fraction statistic. The underlying drift statistic is algebraically retained, and much baseline mathematics is reorganized. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contributions on router-aware stabilization demonstrated on Countdown and mathematics. v2 adds the diagnosis of routing drift, volatile mismatch signals and clipping activity preceding collapse as an explicit central contribution, and extends its effectiveness claims to code benchmarks.

C2.justification: The basic explanation linking router drift, importance-ratio variability and clipping already appears in v1. v2 refines its temporal interpretation, describes entropy as an indicator of policy collapse rather than expert diversity, and adds quantified throughput and memory tradeoffs in Section 5.6.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies layer/expert counts, rollout group size, exact clipping ranges, the default router-shift floor, reward verifiers and code evaluation details. Section 5.6 documents caching costs. Conversely, v2 removes v1's PyTorch snippet, small-model parameter counts, pretraining learning rate, eight-H100 hardware statement and verl implementation disclosure.

R1.justification: The dedicated related-work discussion is largely retained. v2 adds Qin et al.'s Countdown-generation reference and removes the Omni-MATH, DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen2.5 technical-report references. It also more explicitly positions its main instantiation as GMPO plus router-shift weighting.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries, method and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. v2 introduces a standalone diagnosis section and reorganizes technical details, baseline objectives and analyses into Appendices A–E. This substantially changes the document's explanatory structure.

P2.justification: Table 1 becomes a grouped mathematics/code table. v2 adds reward and mechanism-diagnostic plots, combines the plug-in comparisons, adds a stop-gradient plot and removes the router schematic. Existing floor and replay panels are separated and relocated, entropy is redrawn, and captions and page layouts change substantially.

improvement.justification: The routing and clipping diagnostics substantially strengthen the empirical support for v1's largely inferential instability explanation. Code evaluation broadens validation, while explicit configurations, seed reporting and quantified overhead make the evidence and practical costs easier to assess. These gains outweigh the lost implementation snippet and pretraining details, although the relationship between the revised weighting order and unchanged mathematics scores remains unexplained.
